sections.h2: How does property tax work in Casey County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Casey County follows the same statewide cycle as the rest of Kentucky: the PVA assesses on January 1, the sheriff collects from October through April 15, and the county clerk handles whatever is still unpaid afterward. What makes Casey County different is its size and shape. The county covers about 446 square miles, Liberty is its only city, and the 2020 census classed every resident as rural.

That has a direct effect on bills. Nearly every parcel is a farm tract, a hillside lot in the Knobs, or a house along one of the state routes that cross the county, so the assessment is often the main thing worth checking before you list.

sections.h2: Which Casey County office handles which tax question?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about what you owe this year, and the clerk about anything delinquent. The offices below are the ones the county's own pages list.

sections.h2: What is Casey County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
It is a small, spread-out market. The county was formed in 1806 from the western part of Lincoln County, and the present courthouse in Liberty dates to 1888. The 2020 census counted 15,941 people in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, of which 14.9 percent were vacant. About 76 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied, so many sellers are parting with the home they live in.

Casey is described as the only Kentucky county that sits entirely in the Knobs region, and its high point is Green River Knob at 1,789 feet. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. Several routes serve the county, including US 127, KY 80 and KY 49. The Casey County Schools district runs the public schools, and the county's best-known event is the Casey County Apple Festival.

  • Casey sits next to Boyle, Lincoln, Pulaski, Russell, Adair, Taylor and Marion counties.
  • Russell and Adair counties lie on the time zone line to the south and southwest.
  • Liberty is both the seat and the largest city, so city tax questions come up only for in-town homes.

sections.h2: What are the payment steps and penalties in Casey County?
sections.html:
The sheriff's bill sets the amount you pay, and the date you pay it moves the total. Under KRS 134.015, a payment made in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount. From November 2 to December 31 you owe the bill amount. January adds a 5 percent penalty, and from February 1 a 10 percent penalty applies, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.

Taxes are a debt you personally owe from the assessment date, and the delinquency lien stays attached to the land for eleven years even after a sale of the property. The Department of Revenue also notes that if collection starts late, an alternative schedule gives owners 30 days at each stage instead.

Your best move if a bill is lost is to ask the PVA or clerk for the parcel number, then request a copy from the sheriff. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still leaves the bill in your name, so confirm payment before you close.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Casey County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference with the Casey County PVA before the tax roll inspection period ends. The roll is open for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, and the conference can be held by telephone if you ask.

If you still disagree, file a written petition with the county clerk by one workday after the inspection period closes, naming the property and your opinion of its fair cash value. The board of assessment appeals then hears the case 25 to 35 days after the inspection ends. Bring evidence: sales of similar houses, a construction cost record, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. KRS 133.120 says the board must deny an appeal if the owner will not provide reasonable value information when asked.

  • Hold the PVA conference first. Skipping it blocks every later step.
  • Pay tax on the value you claim while the appeal is pending.
  • If the board raises the value, a supplemental bill follows and is due when prepared.

sections.h2: When does a Casey County tax bill go to the delinquent tax sale?
sections.html:
A bill goes to the clerk after April 15 and can be sold to a private buyer at the clerk's yearly sale. For the 2025 bills, the Casey County Clerk reported receiving the sheriff's list on April 16, 2026, advertised the certificates in The Casey County News on July 15, 2026, and scheduled the sale for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am at the clerk's office on Campbellsville Street. That date has passed. Each year's sale follows the same pattern in summer.

Owners can pay right up to the opening of the sale. Buyers must register with the clerk at least ten days ahead and pay the recording fee for each lien assignment, which the clerk lists at $46. Anyone buying more than three certificates in a county, or more than five statewide, also has to register with the Department of Revenue.

A purchased certificate means you now owe the buyer, who may add fees. Paying before the sale avoids that.

sections.h2: Does Casey County have tax relief for older or disabled owners?
sections.html:
Yes. The state homestead exemption subtracts a set dollar amount from the assessed value of the home when the owner is 65 or older or totally disabled. The amount was $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and the Department of Revenue republishes it every two years. File the application with the Casey County PVA, with proof of age such as a driver's license or passport.

Sellers sometimes forget that the exemption belongs to the owner living in the house. If you move into care or sell during the year, tell the PVA so the next bill reflects the change.

sections.h2: How do I close a sale in Casey County when tax is unpaid?
sections.html:
Ask the clerk and the sheriff for written balances, then give both to your closing agent. Any bill still unpaid at closing is subtracted from your proceeds, and a lien filed by the clerk has to be released before the buyer gets clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office, and the clerk's page lists a fee for recording them.

If the home is inherited, vacant, or in poor shape, a cash buyer who takes it as-is can still pay the tax from the price. That keeps you out of the sale in August, when delinquent bills become public record.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

faqs.q: When did the 2026 Casey County tax sale take place?
faqs.a: It was set for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am at the county clerk's office, 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Unpaid 2025 bills could be paid until the sale opened.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky homestead exemption for a Casey County owner?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off the assessed value for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. Apply through the Casey County PVA with proof of age or disability.

faqs.q: Can I appeal if I missed the May inspection period?
faqs.a: Generally no. Kentucky requires the PVA conference and a clerk filing by the end of the inspection period, unless the state approves an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether an extension applied.

faqs.q: Does an unpaid tax bill block a sale of Casey County land?
faqs.a: No, though the bill and any lien must be paid at closing. Get payoff figures from the sheriff or clerk first so the title company can deduct them.
